questions.question: India has an open border with which of the following countries?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nepal**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India shares an **open border** with **Nepal**.
 
• This means that the movement of people between the two countries is largely unrestricted.
 
• The open border facilitates trade, commerce, and cultural exchange between India and Nepal.
 
• **Citizens of both countries can travel without the need for a visa or passport**, adhering to certain identification requirements.
 
• The open border agreement is a significant aspect of the friendly and cooperative relationship between India and Nepal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The India-Nepal open border is established under the **1950 Indo-Nepal Treaty of Peace and Friendship**.
 
• The treaty allows for free movement of people and goods between the two nations and grants reciprocal rights of residence, ownership of property, participation in trade and commerce, and other privileges.
 
• This open border has historical significance and has been in place for decades, reflecting the deep-rooted ties between the two countries.
 
• Despite the open border, both nations have established mechanisms to address security concerns and manage cross-border activities effectively.
 
• The open border is a unique feature of India-Nepal relations and is not common with India's other neighboring countries.

questions.question: In India the financial/fiscal year is taken from _______.

• In India, the financial/fiscal year runs from **1st April to 31st March**.
 
• This period is used for accounting purposes by businesses and the government.
 
• The **fiscal year** is **critical for budgeting, tax assessment, and financial reporting** in India.
 
• Adopting this period aligns with the agricultural cycle in India, which traditionally ends in March, making it easier for farmers and related sectors to report their annual finances.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The financial year in India is important for the preparation of financial statements and reports.
 
• It also plays a significant role in the formulation of the **Union Budget**, which is** presented annually by the Finance Minister**.
 
• Many other countries also follow a similar fiscal year, including the United Kingdom, Canada, and Japan.
 
• Fiscal policies, tax regulations, and government spending are all planned based on this financial year.

questions.question: Which among the following Articles of the Indian Constitution deal with 'Right to Freedom of Religion'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 25-28**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 25-28** of the Indian Constitution deal with the '**Right to Freedom of Religion**'.
 
• These articles ensure that all individuals have the freedom to profess, practice, and propagate their religion.
 
• The provisions under these articles also protect religious practices and allow religious groups to manage their own affairs in matters of religion.
 
• Article 25 guarantees **freedom of conscience** and the right to freely profess, practice, and propagate religion.
 
• Article 26 ensures the** freedom to manage religious affairs**.
 
• Article 27 provides **freedom from payment of taxes **for promotion of any particular religion.
 
• Article 28 allows **freedom from attending religious **instruction or worship in certain educational institutions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Right to Freedom of Religion** is a fundamental right under **Part III** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• These rights are subject to public order, morality, and health, and to other provisions of Part III of the Constitution.
 
• The Constitution of India aims to maintain a balance between the freedom of religion and other fundamental rights to ensure harmony and peace in the society.
 
• India is a secular state, which means that the state treats all religions impartially and does not uphold any religion as the state religion.
 
• **The Constitution of India was adopted on 26th November 1949 and came into effect on 26th January 1950.**
 
• It is the longest written constitution of any country in the world and lays down the framework for political principles, government structure, and the rights and duties of citizens.

questions.question: _________ dance form originates from the southern Indian state of Kerala.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathakali and Mohiniyattam**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kathakali and Mohiniyattam** are traditional dance forms that **originate from Kerala**, a state in southern India.
 
• **Kathakali** is known for its elaborate costumes, makeup, and face masks, and it typically depicts stories from Hindu epics and mythology.
 
• **Mohiniyattam**, which translates to "**dance of the enchantress**," is characterized by graceful, swaying body movements and subtle facial expressions.
 
• Both dance forms are integral to Kerala's cultural heritage and have a significant place in Indian classical dance traditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kathakali** is traditionally performed by **male dancers**, while **Mohiniyattam** is predominantly performed by **female dancers**.
 
• The training for both dance forms is rigorous and involves mastering complex gestures, footwork, and expressions.
 
• Kathakali performances are usually accompanied by vocalists and a percussion ensemble, including instruments like the chenda and maddalam.
 
• Mohiniyattam is typically performed with Carnatic classical music and features instruments like the veena, mridangam, and flute.

questions.question: Who hosted the 2011 ODI cricket world cup?
questions.solution:

__
 
• The 2011 ODI Cricket World Cup was **co-hosted by India, Sri Lanka, and Bangladesh**.
 
• This was the **tenth edition** of the Cricket World Cup, and it was the third time it was held in the Indian subcontinent.
 
• India went on to win the tournament, marking their second World Cup victory, the first being in 1983.
 
• The final match was held at the **Wankhede Stadium in Mumbai, India**, where India defeated Sri Lanka.
 
• The tournament featured a total of **14 teams** competing in 49 matches.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The 2011 Cricket World Cup saw the use of the **Decision Review System (DRS)** for the first time in a World Cup.
 
• It was the first time that Bangladesh co-hosted the World Cup, although India and Sri Lanka had previously co-hosted in 1987 and 1996.
 
• The tournament was notable for the **high-scoring matches** and the performances of several key players, including India's Sachin Tendulkar and Yuvraj Singh, who was named the Player of the Tournament.
 
• The mascot for the 2011 World Cup was **Stumpy**, a young elephant.
 
• The official song of the 2011 Cricket World Cup was "**De Ghuma Ke**", composed by the trio of Shankar–Ehsaan–Loy.

questions.question: In which year did Cripps Mission arrive in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1942**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cripps Mission** arrived in India in **1942** during **World War II**.
 
• The mission was led by **Sir Stafford Cripps**, a member of the British Cabinet.
 
• The purpose of the mission was to secure Indian cooperation and support for the British war efforts.
 
• The mission proposed **Dominion status** for India after the war, but it was rejected by Indian leaders.
 
• Both the Indian National Congress and the Muslim League opposed the proposals, leading to its failure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Cripps Mission** was seen as a last-minute effort by the British to gain Indian support during a critical time in the war.
 
• Its failure led to increased support for the **Quit India Movement** launched by Mahatma Gandhi in August 1942.
 
• The mission is often cited as a significant event in the history of India's struggle for independence.
 
• Despite its failure, the mission highlighted the growing demand for Indian self-governance and eventual independence.
 
• India eventually gained independence on **15th August 1947**.

questions.question: Article ____________ of the Indian Constitution gives an extensive original jurisdiction to the Supreme Court in regard to enforcement of Fundamental Rights.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**32**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 32** of the Indian Constitution provides an extensive original jurisdiction to the Supreme Court in matters related to the **enforcement of Fundamental Rights**.
 
• It is often referred to as the "**heart and soul**" of the Constitution by **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar**, as it provides the right to individuals to move the Supreme Court directly in case of violation of their fundamental rights.
 
• This article** empowers the Supreme Court to issue directions or orders or writs**, including writs in the nature of habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto, and certiorari.
 
• Article 32 is a crucial provision that ensures the protection and enforcement of Fundamental Rights, making the Supreme Court a guardian of these rights.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Supreme Court **of India was **established **on **January 28, 1950**, and is the highest judicial forum and final court of appeal under the Constitution of India.
 
• Fundamental Rights are enshrined in **Part III **of the Indian Constitution, from **Articles 12 to 35**.
 
• Article 32 can be suspended only during the period of **Emergency **as per **Article 359** of the Constitution.
 
• Alongside Article 32, Article 226 also provides the power to High Courts to issue certain writs for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights and for any other purpose.

questions.question: The Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi (Amendment) Bill, 2023 establishes the National Capital Civil Services Authority, which consists of the Chief Minister, Chief Secretary of Delhi and _____________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Principal Home Secretary of Delhi**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi (Amendment) Bill, 2023 **establishes the National Capital Civil Services Authority.
 
• The National Capital Civil Services Authority consists of three members: the Chief Minister of Delhi, the Chief Secretary of Delhi, and the **Principal Home Secretary of Delhi**.
 
• This authority is responsible for making recommendations to the Lieutenant Governor regarding matters concerning transfers and postings of officers and employees of the Delhi government.
 
• The inclusion of the Principal Home Secretary ensures that administrative and internal security aspects are considered in decision-making.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi (Amendment) Bill, 2023 aims to enhance the governance framework of Delhi by clearly defining the roles and responsibilities of various authorities.
 
• The bill seeks to strike a balance between the powers of the elected government of Delhi and the central government represented by the Lieutenant Governor.
 
• It addresses issues related to administrative efficiency and the effective implementation of policies in the National Capital Territory.
 
• This amendment is part of ongoing efforts to streamline the governance of Delhi and ensure better coordination between various levels of government.
 
• By including key officials in the National Capital Civil Services Authority, the bill aims to provide a more structured and accountable mechanism for administrative decisions.

questions.question: Which of the following gases, when cooled and compressed, can change from a gas to a supercritical fluid state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Carbon dioxide (CO₂)**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Carbon dioxide (CO₂)** can transition to a supercritical fluid state when cooled and compressed beyond its critical temperature and pressure.
 
• A supercritical fluid is a state of matter where distinct liquid and gas phases do not exist.
 
• Supercritical CO2 is commonly used in various industrial applications, including supercritical fluid extraction and as a solvent in chemical processes.
 
• The critical temperature and pressure for **CO₂ are 31.1°C and 73.8 atm**, respectively.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Supercritical fluids** have properties of both liquids and gases, making them versatile in various scientific and industrial processes.
 
• The use of supercritical CO₂ is favored for its** non-toxic, non-flammable nature** and its ability to act as a solvent without the need for hazardous chemicals.
 
• Other gases can also become supercritical fluids under the right conditions, but CO₂ is one of the most commonly utilized due to its relatively low critical temperature and pressure.
 
• Understanding the behavior of supercritical fluids is important in fields such as materials science, chemistry, and engineering.

questions.question: Article 43 ∶ The State shall endeavour to promote cottage industries on an individual or cooperative basis in rural are it is a Directive based on _____ Principles.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gandhian**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 43** of the Indian Constitution is based on **Gandhian principles**.
 
• This article directs the state to promote **cottage industries** on an individual or cooperative basis in rural areas.
 
• It aims to improve the economic conditions of rural areas by encouraging small-scale, traditional industries.
 
• The **promotion of cottage industries** aligns with Mahatma Gandhi's vision of a self-reliant rural economy.
 
• This directive principle is part of the broader goal to achieve social and economic democracy in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)** are guidelines for the framing of laws by the government, provided in** Part IV** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• They are not enforceable by any court, but they are considered fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
• The DPSPs aim to create social and economic conditions under which the citizens can lead a good life.
 
• They also aim to establish social and economic democracy through a welfare state.
 
• **Article 43** reflects the **Gandhian ideology** of promoting rural development and self-sufficiency.
 
• Other Gandhian principles in the DPSPs include the** promotion of village panchayats** (**Article 40**) and the prohibition of intoxicating drinks and drugs (Article 47).
